title: Harmonized Intent Surface PRD + Launch Acceptance Checklist
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Customers maintain multiple integration paths for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank, increasing SDK complexity and causing inconsistent behavior across features. Goal: Ship a harmonized, intent-driven Hosted API surface that lets a single endpoint accept an explicit 'intent' field and optional hints, and routes requests to the optimal serving path (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) with deterministic fallback and transparent billing. This ticket defines the PRD, success criteria, and launch checklist for the minimum-safe launch of the Harmonized Intent Surface.
requirements: Introduce /v1/infer/intent endpoint that accepts a unified envelope: {intent, mode_hints, model_preference, input, response_schema, streaming}.
Intent values supported at launch: "chat", "completion", "embedding", "rerank". Endpoint may map certain intents to existing specialized endpoints internally.
Routing decision must be deterministic and logged. Each request must include a routing_decision id in response headers for traceability.
Preserve existing behavioral contracts for legacy endpoints (backwards-compatibility for customers not using the new surface).
Support streaming responses for chat and completion intents with the same chunking model as existing streaming endpoints.
Return embeddings in the same vector format and dimensionality as existing embeddings endpoint; rerank must accept a candidate list and return scores identical to /v1/rerank semantics.
Expose a compatibility mode flag for customers to opt-out of automatic intent remapping and route to legacy behavior.
Instrument per-intent metrics (requests, p95 latency, errors, model_version, tokens_in, tokens_out) and hook them into Console dashboards and alerting.
Billing must be clear: responses must include token_count breakdown and charge_preview header linking to cost-estimate API for the chosen model variant.
Document migration path: sample SDK calls, cURL examples, and a deprecation plan for legacy endpoint aliases (if applicable).
acceptance_criteria: Functional: /v1/infer/intent accepts unified envelope and returns correct typed response for each intent in automated suite (100% pass on feature tests).

Latency: P95 server-side latency for completion intent <= 120ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) on hosted-tier-1 models; chat streaming must begin emitting first chunk within 200ms of request acceptance for typical prompts.

Correctness: Embedding vectors match legacy /v1/embeddings for same model and input (L2 distance < 1e-6 for deterministic models); rerank scores preserve ordering for canonical dataset (Spearman rho >= 0.98 compared to legacy rerank).
Billing: token_count header matches post-processing billing pipeline for a sample suite of requests and charge_preview header returns consistent estimate within 2% of final invoice for those samples.
Observability: Per-intent dashboards populate within 24 hours of rollout and at least two alert rules are active (error-rate spike and latency breach).

Security & compliance: KMS-integrated key wrapping works for Private deployments; audit events include routing_decision id and are retained per retention policy. Security review completed and signed off by security reviewer Priya Kapoor.
Backward compatibility: Customers using legacy endpoints see no change unless they opt into unified surface; migration docs validated by Solutions Engineering with at least two pilot customers.
launch_checklist: Code: Merge feature branch and land runtime changes (PR #redwood/infer/intent-rf) - engineering owner: Nina Rao.
Integration tests: Run full cross-intent e2e suite against staging runtime; must pass 100%.
Canary rollout: 1% traffic for 48 hours, then 5% for 72 hours, monitoring error rate and latency per-intent.
Pilot customers: Onboard 2 pilot customers to opt-in to the unified endpoint and collect integration feedback within pilot period.
Docs: Publish migration guide, SDK examples (Python/Node), and API reference before canary begins. Docs owner: Samir Patel (DX).
Console: Add per-intent default dashboard tile and a routing_decision header drilldown link to request logs.
Billing: Coordinate with Finance to ensure charge_preview header is enabled for canary billing reconciliation.
Security: Complete threat model update and sign-off from Security; perform KMS integration test for Private clusters.
Support: Prepare runbook for operational issues and FAQ for common integration errors; support triage owner: Lars Jensen.
Rollback plan: Automated toggle to revert routing for the unified endpoint and map traffic back to legacy endpoints in <15 minutes without data loss.
out_of_scope: Auto-detecting intent purely from user text (NLP intent classification) is deferred — we require explicit intent from callers at launch.
Merging billing models or introducing a new pricing tier in this launch. Any pricing changes will be handled in a follow-up release.
Deep compositional orchestration (splitting a single request across multiple models) is out of scope for the initial roll-out.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Require explicit 'intent' field rather than auto-classification to avoid surprising routing and billing — chosen for predictability and auditability.
Tradeoff: Unified envelope simplifies SDK surface but adds routing overhead in the fronting layer; we will cache routing decisions and optimize hot-paths to reduce added latency.
Decision: Streaming behavior aligned with existing streaming endpoints; we will not change chunk semantics to minimize client rework.
Tradeoff: Preserving deterministic embedding outputs constrains allowed model quantization for some hosted tiers; we will roll quantized variants under distinct model names to avoid surprise deltas.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers may mis-specify intent and get degraded results. Mitigation: Provide explicit SDK validators and verbose error messages suggesting the correct intent, plus a compatibility-mode flag.

Risk: Increased latency from fronting routing logic. Mitigation: Benchmark routing path, add in-memory routing cache, and add fallback to serve from legacy endpoint when latency budget would be exceeded.
Risk: Billing mismatch during canary. Mitigation: Reconcile canary billing with Finance daily and disable charge_preview if discrepancies detected.
open_questions: Should the unified endpoint accept multipart/batch requests (multiple inputs per call) at launch or wait for next iteration?
Do we add an explicit "model_preference" hierarchy or only a single model string in the envelope? Current plan: single model string; possible iteration to preference list post-launch.
What SLAs (if any) do we guarantee for the unified endpoint beyond existing endpoint SLAs? Proposed: match existing per-endpoint SLAs and document them.

migration_plan_summary: Dual-run period where clients can opt-in. Provide SDK flag `use_unified_intent=true`. After 3 consecutive months of zero opt-ins for legacy aliases and no active enterprise blockers, schedule a deprecation announcement with 90-day sunset. Solutions Eng to run two customer pilots during canary period.
notes: Keep the explicit intent requirement prominent in landing docs to avoid accidental routing and billing issues.
We will revisit batch/multi-input in Q3 2025 based on pilot feedback and demand.
